# The Lights That Keep Their Promise

## Scripture
"I have set my rainbow in the clouds, and it will be the sign of the covenant between me and the earth." — Genesis 9:13

## Reflection
October evenings bring earlier darkness, and with it, clearer skies. If you look toward the northeast on a crisp autumn night, you may glimpse the Andromeda Galaxy—a faint smudge of light that has traveled 2.5 million years to reach your eyes. It never flickers or fails. It simply keeps shining, exactly as it always has, exactly as it always will.

That constancy echoes an older promise. After the flood, God hung a rainbow in the clouds—not as a fleeting beauty, but as a lasting sign. Every covenant-keeper knows: God does not make promises lightly, and He does not break them quietly.

The autumn sky preaches this same sermon. Seasons shift, leaves fall, temperatures drop—yet the galaxies hold their courses. The heavens declare a faithfulness that outlasts our feelings and outpaces our fears.

Perhaps tonight you feel the chill of uncertainty. Maybe a promise of God seems distant, buried under clouds of doubt. But the light still travels. The covenant still stands. The One who set the rainbow in the clouds also set the stars in their places—and neither has ever failed to appear.

## Prayer
Father, when the night feels long and Your promises seem far off, remind me that You are the God who keeps covenant. Your faithfulness reaches beyond the clouds, beyond the years, beyond everything I can see. Help me to trust the light that is still traveling toward me. Amen.
